summary: This class explains the custom of having impoverished Hahamim study Zohar and Tehillim during the Shiva to elevate the Neshama of the deceased. It covers the daily reading, known as Qiraya or Qirayat, the final day of the week with speeches and a meat dinner in the Beit Evel, and the transition over time to reading Tehillim.
questions: Who studied Torah in the house of the mourners during the Shiva?
What books were traditionally read during the Shiva?
What happened at the culmination of each day's Qiraya at the end of the week?
Why did Tehillim eventually replace the Zohar in many circles?
When was the final day's gathering held if the sixth day fell on Shabbat?
